summary: This benchmark evaluates whether paired link-edit training improves counterfactual recall in compact convolutional and recurrent neural routing hosts under a fixed 128-update budget. The empirical results show that paired training marginally degrades clean accuracy and fails to achieve targeted 90% edit accuracy, though a post hoc direct-readout diagnostic reveals that routing locators retain relevant location information. The study provides rigorous experimental controls and detailed hardware/software specifications, though its domain context and broader applicability remain constrained by its synthetic design.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls including matched update budgets, identical donor starting points, and native from-scratch baselines.
Transparent reporting of negative and null results with 95% confidence intervals derived from whole-program resampling.

Comprehensive environmental specification documenting hardware (Apple M5 Ultra), execution time (62.52s), memory footprint (302 MB), and exact software library versions (MLX 0.32.4, Python 3.12.16, NumPy 2.5.5).
Insightful post hoc diagnostic demonstrating that locator accuracy significantly outperforms the neural decoder readout on explicit payloads.
weaknesses: Dense, shorthand prose that omits foundational context regarding the specific register-routing task formulation, making self-contained interpretation difficult without external documentation.
Evaluation is restricted to a single donor router and objective function on synthetic program streams, limiting generalizability to broader model-editing settings.
No formally attached code repository in the submission metadata, qualifying the article only for the text_only badge.
suggestions: Provide a brief conceptual diagram or introductory paragraph defining the register-routing task structure, links, and query types within the body text.
Investigate the mechanistic cause of decoder failure compared to locator success (e.g., representational drift or catastrophic interference in the decoder layers).
Expand testing to multiple donor architectures or scaling variations beyond the 60-write program length.

claims.text: The CPU training and evaluation ran in 62.52 seconds on an Apple M5 Ultra, peaking at 302 MB resident memory, using Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4 and NumPy 2.5.5.
claims.source: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/releases (MLX 0.32.4 released Oct 2026 for Apple silicon including M5 architectures)

claims.text: Under the same 128 target updates, paired edit training lowered clean accuracy by 0.48–1.32 percentage points and failed to reach 90% on either edit metric in either host on fresh programs.
claims.source: Empirically documented within the submission's reported benchmark tables and confidence intervals

claims.text: A post hoc readout change reached 90.57–90.84% on current-link edits among correct clean queries using the clean-only router.
claims.source: Empirically documented within the submission's hard readout diagnostic analysis
